Launch page — revised messaging package (version 5; draft for review, not published)

Documented rationale
The launch context records low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves. This revision makes the intended audience explicit and uses an AI-manager framing instead of generic AI-for-business language. The goal is to relaunch with messaging that converts one-person-company founders; this draft does not claim that the revision has caused lift.

Scope
This package covers the launch-page messaging for the relaunch: audience definition, headline, subhead, primary call to action, supporting copy, audience-fit section, message promises, and review/measurement criteria. It is a review draft only and must not be published or sent from this artifact.

Intended audience
One-person-company founders and lean SME operators, especially people carrying multiple business functions and looking for practical help coordinating business work with the resources they already have.

Headline
"Run your one-person company with an AI manager."

Subhead
"Somebody helps you keep the work moving across your business—so you can spend less time coordinating and more time serving customers."

Primary call to action
"Meet your AI manager"

Supporting copy
You are the founder, operator, and decision-maker. Somebody is an AI manager for your one-person company: a way to help keep business work organised and moving without adding another person to your team.

Whether you are handling customer work, follow-ups, planning, or the next task on your list, start with a clearer picture of what needs attention and what to do next.

Who this is for
- Founders running a one-person company.
- Lean SME operators who are carrying the work of multiple business functions.
- People looking for practical help coordinating business work with the resources they already have.

What this message promises
- A clear fit for one-person-company founders.
- An AI-manager framing rather than generic "AI for your business" language.
- Help with coordinating business work using the resources already available to the operator.

Required launch assets and copy
- The launch-page headline, subhead, primary CTA, supporting copy, audience section, and promise section above.
- The relaunch page must display the complete package consistently; no additional paid asset is specified in the supplied records.
- Measurement instrumentation for page visits, CTA interaction, signup completion, and an audience-recognition signal must be available before or at relaunch so the criteria below can be assessed.

Acceptance criteria
Before or during relaunch, all of the following must be true:
1. The page displays one headline, one subhead, one primary CTA, the supporting copy, the audience section, and the message-promises section from this package; review confirms no section is missing.
2. The headline and audience copy explicitly identify one-person-company founders, and the page uses the AI-manager framing; review confirms both are present.
3. The primary CTA is present and its interaction is measurable; CTA interaction and signup completion events are recorded for the relaunch period.
4. Signup conversion is measured for the relaunch period and compared with the current low-conversion signal; no improvement or causal lift is claimed until quantitative results are collected.
5. An audience-recognition signal is collected during the relaunch because the current record says visitors do not recognise themselves; the signal and segment-level results must be reviewed before stronger messaging conclusions are made.
6. Any numeric target or comparison baseline not supplied in the company records remains to be set by the reviewer; this draft does not invent a success threshold.

Review status
Draft for review, not published. Review the explicit one-person-company-founder framing against the current page, verify the required copy and measurement instrumentation, then collect quantitative signup and segment-level results before making stronger causal or lift claims.

Unsupported hypotheses / not established by the evidence
- That generic audience framing is the sole cause of low signup conversion.
- That the assumed pain point of "too many tools" is a validated customer pain point.
- That a specific alternative headline or subhead will improve conversion.
- Any numerical conversion effect, traffic effect, segment difference, or causal lift; the record provides none of these.

Relaunch diagnostic focus
- Replace generic "business" language with specific one-person-company-founder language, then measure signup conversion against the current page.
- Preserve the distinction between the observed signal and hypotheses until quantitative experiment and segment-level results are available.
- Operating constraint: no paid spend without an explicit application-approved provider path.
- Leave this draft for review; do not send or publish it from this assignment.
